scenario: A courier platform analyzes riders only if they deliver more than 40 parcels in a day. Operations wants the mean daily parcel count across all riders.

data.description: Only daily counts above 40 are observed. Parcel count is Normal with known sigma 10.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean parcel count mu across all riders and (b) the fraction of riders observed.
naive_answer: Average rider output is about 44.39 parcels because that is the observed mean.
naive_trap: Only high-output riders are in the analysis set.
reasoning_trace: Alpha≈1.5 implies mu=40-1.5*10=25 and observed fraction near 0.0668.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(40-mu)/10; return mu+10*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-44.39
mu=brentq(eq,-20,39.99)
frac=norm.sf((40-mu)/10)
assert abs(mu-25)<0.5 and abs(frac-0.0668)<0.005
